acceptanceCriteria: A retained receipt of the full ContextBench run reports file and line-span recall, precision and bytes against the adapter's baselines.
A preregistered paired trial on a SWE-bench Pro subset reports resolve rate, tokens and cost for the same model and budget with and without Corvint.
Results, including a null or negative result, are recorded in BUILD-LOG and the README status table.
body: Filed 2026-09-27 from the owner-requested gap analysis of Corvint against competing context tools, current standards and a trial on a local clone of MeVille (TypeScript, about 4,600 tracked files). Corvint has no published outcome number on repositories it was not tuned on: blind-v2 recall 0.071 and blind-v3 recall 0.18 on first runs, the latest held-out attempt returned forbidden results on 7 of 36 must-exclude checks (README.md:370), and the CEM reviewer pilot scored 0.86 against 0.90 (README.md:372). Competitors publish numbers (Cursor Context Bench, SWE-grep weighted F1, Bugbot resolution rate, codebase-memory 83% vs 92% at 10x fewer tokens). The ContextBench adapter exists (decision 0372) but the full run is NOT_RUN (docs/BUILD-LOG.md:1778). SWE-bench Verified is not a credible headline: OpenAI retired it in February 2026. V1-0220 covers a rerunnable public harness; this ticket is the measured result.
title: eval: run the full ContextBench sample and a paired SWE-bench Pro trial with and without Corvint, reporting tokens and cost
